questions.question: Is Nagavally or Sreedevi a foil to Ganga? Substantiate
questions.solution_html:
• Sreedevi is the opposite of Ganga, village raised, believes in traditions and
  • superstitions, obeys customs, confined to the Meda; while Ganga is city bred,
  • inquisitive, disobeys. Nagavalli is an extension of Ganga rather than an opposite,
  • one who transcends Ganga’s limits, she appears contrary but really is a
  • complimentary aspect of Ganga /(CO2)

questions.question: Attempt a brief theoretical reading of Amen as a text that blends magical realism with local folklore traditions.
questions.solution_html:
• Amen skillfully blends the stylistic tenets of magical realism with the rooted
  • traditions of Kerala's local folklore and Nasrani (Syrian Christian) culture. Set in the
  • mythical village of Kumarankari, the film creates an ethereal, "dreamy" atmosphere
  • where the supernatural is integrated into the daily lives of the villagers as a matter-
  • of-fact reality. The intervention of the divine, the portrayal of St. George, etc are
  • some of the elements of magic realism /(CO4)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: some of the elements of magic realism /(CO4)

questions.question: ‘Swaroopam is about a villager whose life was turned upside down due to his sudden fixation with an imagined past.’ Critically evaluate this statement.
questions.solution_html:
• The film Swaroopam (1992) is a sombre character study on how a sudden,
  • misplaced pride in a romanticized, "imagined" past can destroy a perfectly
  • functional present, turning a responsible man (the protagonist, Sekharan) into a
  • delusional, irresponsible figure. The film serves as a psychological and social
  • critique of how nostalgia, elite delusions, and the pursuit of "imagined" ancestral
  • glory can destroy practical, hardworking lives. /(CO1)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: glory can destroy practical, hardworking lives. /(CO1)

questions.question: What does Ganga’s transformation suggest about memory, identity, and the psychological burden of inherited stories?
questions.solution_html:
• Ganga’s transformation into Nagavalli in the 1993 film Manichitrathazhu suggests
  • that memory is a malleable, often dangerous reservoir of unprocessed trauma; that
  • identity is fragile and constructed through personal and cultural narratives; and that
  • inherited stories, particularly feudal tales of oppression and gendered violence, can
  • exert a heavy, triggering burden on the modern, psychological self. /(CO2)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: exert a heavy, triggering burden on the modern, psychological self. /(CO2)

questions.question: Critically evaluate Perariyathavar as both an ecological film and a political statement on caste.
questions.solution_html:
• Dr. Biju’s Perariyathavar (2015) is a significant piece of Malayalam "eco-social
  • realism" that functions simultaneously as a poignant ecological film and a scathing
  • political critique of caste in India. By focusing on the lives of two municipal
  • sweepers, a temporary cleaner and his child, the film highlights the invisibility of
  • marginalized labourers and the environmental degradation they are forced to
  • inhabit. The inseparability of waste and marginalisation, caste and labour, state
  • apathy, displacement all become themes. /(CO3)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: apathy, displacement all become themes. /(CO3)

questions.question: Drishyam is a visualisation of the conflict between the state and the public. Comment.
questions.solution_html:
• Drishyam is a powerful visualization of the conflict between the state, represented
  • by the police and legal system and the public, represented by an ordinary citizen
  • fighting for his family's survival. The film operates as a cat-and-mouse game that
  • highlights the power dynamics between institutional authority and individual,
  • resourcefulness, shifting the traditional perspective of "justice" to a, often legally
  • ambiguous, moral ground. It caters to the public notion that state machinery is
  • failing and it is up to the individual to uphold justice and moral order. (CO 4)
